title: Web app design
metaDescription: Web app design services for complex products: information architecture, workflows, and interfaces that stay simple as features grow.

hero.h1: Web app design services for complex products that stay simple
hero.sub: Information architecture, workflows, and interfaces for web applications that need to handle complexity without feeling complex.

summary: Information architecture, workflows, and UI for complex web applications.
sourceContext: US UI/UX design agency; this page sells design engagements for logged-in web applications with complex workflows, tables and permissions.
abstract: Web app design services plan the information architecture (IA), workflows and user interface (UI) of logged-in web applications, for example admin consoles, customer portals and software as a service (SaaS) products. Our web app design takes 8–16 weeks, costs $60,000–$180,000, and ends with a component library and developer-ready Figma files.

sections.answer: Web app design is the user experience (UX) and UI design of software that runs in a browser after sign-in, for example a customer relationship management (CRM) tool or an admin console. Designers structure navigation, workflows, data tables and permissions for repeated daily use.
sections.body: Web application design differs from UI UX web design in purpose: a marketing website converts visitors, while a web app supports users who complete the same tasks every day. Web app UI therefore prioritizes speed, keyboard access and clear system states over storytelling.

sections.h2: What does web app design include?
sections.answer: Our web app design services include 6 deliverables: workflow research, an information architecture, wireframes, a clickable prototype, a web app UI kit and a design handoff package.

items.title: Workflow research.
items.body: Interviews and task analysis with 5–8 users per role, for example admins, managers and operators.

items.title: Information architecture.
items.body: A navigation model and sitemap validated with tree testing in Optimal Workshop, for example 10–15 tasks per test.

items.title: Wireframes.
items.body: Low-fidelity screens for every workflow, for example list views, detail views, forms and settings.

items.title: Clickable prototype.
items.body: A Figma prototype tested with 5 users per round in Maze, for example a 5-task test of the core workflow.

items.title: Web app UI kit.
items.body: Components for complex screens, for example data tables, filters, bulk actions, empty states and permission states.

items.title: Design handoff package.
items.body: Annotated Figma files, responsive breakpoints and component specs mapped to Storybook, for example 3 breakpoints at 1280, 1440 and 1920 px.

sections.h2: How does the web app design process work?
sections.answer: The web app design process takes 8–16 weeks (40–80 working days) and runs in 6 steps, from discovery to design handoff.

items.title: Discovery and workflow research (5–10 days)
items.body: We interview users per role, map current workflows as Jobs to be Done and agree the success metrics.

items.title: Information architecture (5–10 days)
items.body: Designers build the navigation model and validate the navigation model with card sorting and tree testing.

items.title: Wireframes and prototype (10–20 days)
items.body: Designers wireframe every workflow and build a clickable Figma prototype of the core tasks.

items.title: Usability testing (5–10 days)
items.body: Each round tests 5 users on the core tasks and scores the prototype with the System Usability Scale (SUS).

items.title: Visual UI and component library (10–20 days)
items.body: Designers apply the brand, build the web app UI kit and check every screen against Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 level AA.

items.title: Design handoff (5–10 days)
items.body: We hand over Figma files and component specs, then review the first builds with developers.

sections.h2: What are the benefits of web app design?
sections.answer: Web app design has 4 benefits: it increases feature adoption, improves task efficiency, reduces training time and develops a scalable component library.

items.title: Increases feature adoption
items.body: Clear navigation and discoverable actions increase the share of users who use each new feature.

items.title: Improves task efficiency
items.body: Keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions and saved filters improve the speed of repeated daily tasks.

items.title: Reduces training time
items.body: Consistent patterns across screens reduce the hours new users spend learning the web app.

items.title: Develops a scalable component library
items.body: Each release adds tested components to one library, so the web app UI develops without one-off screens.

sections.h2: Web app design vs UI UX web design
sections.answer: Web app design structures logged-in workflows for repeated use; UI UX web design shapes marketing websites that convert visitors. Products with a public site and a signed-in app need both services.

sections.h2: How much does web app design cost?
sections.answer: Web app design costs $60,000–$180,000 and takes 8–16 weeks. The price depends on 4 factors: the number of workflows, the number of user roles, the number of test rounds and the size of the component library.
sections.body: A web app with 5–6 workflows and 2 user roles sits near $60,000. A web app with 20 or more workflows, 5 user roles, 3 test rounds and a full component library sits near $180,000. Teams that build a new product from zero compare scope with digital product design services.

sections.h2: When should a software company hire web app design services?
sections.answer: A software company should hire web app design services in 5 situations:
items: A new web application is planned, if the team has engineers and no product designer.
Support tickets rise, if users cannot find core features.
New features ship every sprint, if each feature adds a one-off screen.
Enterprise buyers ask for roles and permissions, if the current UI has a single user type.
An accessibility requirement applies, for example a WCAG 2.2 AA clause in a procurement contract.

sections.answer: These answers cover the 5 questions buyers ask most about web app design services.

faqs.q: Is web app design different from website design?
faqs.a: Yes. Web app design supports signed-in users who repeat tasks daily, while website design converts visitors on marketing pages.

faqs.q: Do you design data tables and permissions?
faqs.a: Yes. Web app design covers data tables, filters, bulk actions, user roles and permission states for every workflow in scope.

faqs.q: Does web app design include responsive layouts?
faqs.a: Yes. Web app design includes responsive layouts for 3 desktop breakpoints and mobile layouts for the tasks users complete on a phone.

faqs.q: Can you redesign an existing web app in phases?
faqs.a: Yes. A phased web app redesign starts with the highest-traffic workflow and ships one workflow per release.

faqs.q: How long does web app design take?
faqs.a: Web app design takes 8–16 weeks, which equals 40–80 working days, from discovery to design handoff.
